newsitem.title: USA: Spiegel expects to see "trends improve".
newsitem.headline: Spiegel expects to see "trends improve".

text.p: Spiegel Inc said Wednesday its loss for the second quarter was due mostly to its struggling Spiegel Catalog division, but the company expected trends to improve in the second half of the year.
Spiegel has been working to reposition the catalog and expected "to begin seeing trends improve in the second half of this year," James Sievers, chief financial officer, said in a statement.

Earlier Spiegel said it lost $13.5 million, $0.11 a share, in the second quarter, compared to a loss of $3.3 million, or $0.03 a share, in the same period last year. Sales rose to $696.2 million from $668.6 million.

Finance revenue for the second quarter rose by 16 percent to $38.7 million, including a $19.7 million pre-tax gain on the sale of receivables that was offset somewhat by lower finance revenues generated as a result of lower average level of owned customer receivables.

Selling, general and administrative expenses were 38.0 percent of total revenues during the second quarter compared to 36.9 percent a year ago. The rise reflected $10 million in expenses from the streamlining of Spiegel Catalog operations and the reduction of 125 workers.
